original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')       and i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH store_state AS (
    SELECT s_state, COUNT(*)::bigint AS store_cnt
    FROM store
    GROUP BY s_state
),
filtered_item AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
      AND i_manager_id IN (3, 15, 17, 26, 43, 44, 55, 70, 82, 95)
),
filtered_customer AS (
    SELECT c.c_customer_sk,
           c.c_current_cdemo_sk,
           c.c_current_hdemo_sk
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca
      ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'LA', 'NE', 'NM', 'OH')
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count,
    SUM(st.store_cnt)::bigint AS cnt
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
 AND d1.d_date >= DATE '2001-01-01'
 AND d1.d_date <  DATE '2002-01-01'
JOIN filtered_item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
JOIN filtered_customer c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30' day
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
JOIN store_state st
  ON st.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The original join 'store' only matches on s_state = w_state, multiplying every result row by the number of stores in that state. Since store columns are not used in output or grouping, replace the join with a pre-aggregated store count per state and use SUM(store_cnt), preserving the exact row multiplicities of COUNT(*).

Early-filter customers by ca_state through a CTE joining customer and customer_address, so the fact tables only join against the reduced customer set. Similarly pre-filter items by category and manager_id.

Add implied date bounds: d1.d_date within 2001 and d2.d_date within [2001-01-01, 2002-01-30], which are logically implied by d1.d_year = 2001 and the 30-day window. These extra sargable predicates help prune date_dim and can improve index usage.
Convert implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs, making join order and semantics clearer and enabling the optimizer to propagate filtered dimension keys (item/customer) before fact joins.

original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Electronics', 'Jewelry', 'Music')       and i_manager_id IN (6, 10, 21, 31, 34, 57, 70, 73, 85, 96)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('FL', 'MO', 'PA', 'SC', 'TX')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 31 AND 51     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count,
    SUM(ssc.store_cnt)::bigint AS cnt
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
JOIN item i
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
 AND i.i_category IN ('Electronics', 'Jewelry', 'Music')
 AND i.i_manager_id IN (6, 10, 21, 31, 34, 57, 70, 73, 85, 96)
JOIN customer c
  ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON c.c_current_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
 AND ca.ca_state IN ('FL', 'MO', 'PA', 'SC', 'TX')
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
JOIN warehouse w
  ON inv.inv_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
JOIN (
    SELECT s_state, COUNT(*) AS store_cnt
    FROM store
    GROUP BY s_state
) ssc
  ON ssc.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 31 AND 51
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30 days'
GROUP BY cd.cd_gender, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status, hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Rewrote implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI JOINs with filters placed in the join conditions where appropriate; this preserves semantics but avoids ambiguity and improves maintainability.

The original store join (s_state = w_state) is not connected by a store key, so it multiplies every qualifying row by the number of stores in the warehouse state. It was replaced with a pre-aggregated store count per state and SUM(store_cnt), which is equivalent for the final COUNT(*) aggregation but avoids row multiplication before grouping.
Avoided excessive CTE creation because most filters can be inlined and pushed down by the optimizer. A single derived table is used only for the store-state pre-aggregation.
The 30-day date range condition between d1 and d2 was moved into the join condition and normalized using INTERVAL '30 days' syntax.
The redundant equivalence chain ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk was simplified by joining inventory to warehouse and web_sales to the same warehouse row.
The interval expression d1.d_date + interval '30' day was rewritten as d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30 days' for clearer and more portable interval handling.

original_query: select      cd_gender,     cd_marital_status,     cd_education_status,     hd_vehicle_count,     count(*) as cnt from     store_sales,     web_sales,     date_dim d1,     date_dim d2,     customer,     inventory,     store,     warehouse,     item,     customer_demographics,     household_demographics,     customer_address     where       ss_item_sk = i_item_sk       and ws_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk       and ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk 			and d2.d_date between d1.d_date and (d1.d_date + interval '30' day)       and ss_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_bill_customer_sk = c_customer_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = inv_warehouse_sk       and ws_warehouse_sk = w_warehouse_sk       and inv_item_sk = ss_item_sk       and inv_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk       and inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss_quantity       and s_state = w_state       AND i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')       and i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)       and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk       and c_current_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk       and c_current_addr_sk = ca_address_sk       and ca_state in ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')       and d1.d_year = 2001       and ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28     group by cd_gender, cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, hd_vehicle_count     order by cnt     ;
rewritten_query:
WITH store_state_counts AS (
    SELECT s_state, COUNT(*) AS store_cnt
    FROM store
    GROUP BY s_state
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count,
    SUM(ssc.store_cnt) AS cnt
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN web_sales ws
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 8 AND 28
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '30 days'
 AND d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'
JOIN customer c
  ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
 AND ca.ca_state IN ('AL', 'MI', 'MS', 'OH', 'TX')
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON c.c_current_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
JOIN item i
  ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
 AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Children', 'Men')
 AND i.i_manager_id IN (9, 24, 27, 41, 59, 66, 78, 80, 83, 100)
JOIN warehouse w
  ON ws.ws_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
JOIN store_state_counts ssc
  ON ssc.s_state = w.w_state
JOIN inventory inv
  ON inv.inv_warehouse_sk = ws.ws_warehouse_sk
 AND inv.inv_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND inv.inv_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
 AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand >= ss.ss_quantity
GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    hd.hd_vehicle_count
ORDER BY cnt;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The join `store s ON s_state = w_state` (uncorrelated with store_sales) is a small cross join that multiplies every qualifying row by the number of stores in the warehouse's state. Replaced it with a pre-aggregated `store_state_counts` (one row per state) and changed `COUNT(*)` to `SUM(store_cnt)`, which is mathematically equivalent while removing row expansion entirely (score 9/10).
Converted implicit comma joins into explicit ANSI INNER JOINs, making the join graph unambiguous and allowing the optimizer to reorder freely (score 3/10).

Added the implied redundant predicate `d2.d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-01-01' AND DATE '2002-01-30'` — since d1.d_year=2001 and d2 is within 30 days after d1, d2 must fall in this range. This gives the planner an extra opportunity to filter d2 early (score 5/10).
Pushed selective dimension filters (d_year, i_category, i_manager_id, ca_state, ws_wholesale_cost) directly into JOIN ON clauses so they are applied during the join rather than after (score 4/10).
Added transitive equality `ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk` explicitly in the web_sales join to give the optimizer a direct fact-to-fact join edge on customer key (score 4/10).

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_REFUNDED_CASH) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2001 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 236 and 295 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 28 AND 31 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('MI', 'NC', 'WI') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('W', 'W') and cd_education_status IN ('4 yr Degree', 'College') and cd_gender = 'M' and c_birth_month = 5 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1950 AND 1956 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
with customer_total_return as (
    select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk,
           sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk,
           sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk,
           sum(sr_refunded_cash) as ctr_total_return
    from store_returns
    join date_dim on sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk
    where d_year = 2001
      and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 236 and 295
    group by sr_customer_sk, sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk
),
store_avg_return as (
    select ctr_store_sk,
           avg(ctr_total_return) as avg_total_return
    from customer_total_return
    group by ctr_store_sk
)
select c.c_customer_id
from customer_total_return ctr1
join store_avg_return sa on ctr1.ctr_store_sk = sa.ctr_store_sk
join store s on s.s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk
join customer c on c.c_customer_sk = ctr1.ctr_customer_sk
join customer_demographics cd on c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
where ctr1.ctr_total_return > sa.avg_total_return * 1.2
  and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk between 28 and 31
  and s.s_state in ('MI', 'NC', 'WI')
  and cd.cd_marital_status = 'W'
  and cd.cd_education_status in ('4 yr Degree', 'College')
  and cd.cd_gender = 'M'
  and c.c_birth_month = 5
  and c.c_birth_year between 1950 and 1956
order by c.c_customer_id
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated scalar subquery computing avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 per store with a pre-aggregated store-level CTE (store_avg_return) joined to ctr1. This eliminates repeated CTE scans (O(N*M) -> O(N+M)).
Convert implicit comma joins to explicit JOIN syntax for readability and better join-order control.
Simplify redundant predicate cd_marital_status IN ('W', 'W') to cd_marital_status = 'W'.

Preserve the window semantics of the average (computed over all reasons per store) by aggregating store_avg_return from the unfiltered customer_total_return, then apply ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 28 AND 31 only in the outer query.

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_RETURN_AMT) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2001 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 182 and 241 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 24 AND 27 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('IA', 'NE', 'TX') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('S', 'U') and cd_education_status IN ('Secondary', '4 yr Degree') and cd_gender = 'F' and c_birth_month = 6 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1934 AND 1940 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
with customer_total_return as (
    select sr.sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk,
           sr.sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk,
           sum(sr.sr_return_amt) as ctr_total_return
    from store_returns sr
    join date_dim d on sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    join store s on s.s_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
    where d.d_year = 2001
      and s.s_state in ('IA', 'NE', 'TX')
      and sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity between 182 and 241
    group by sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_store_sk, sr.sr_reason_sk
),
store_avg as (
    select ctr_store_sk,
           avg(ctr_total_return) as avg_ctr_total_return
    from customer_total_return
    group by ctr_store_sk
)
select c.c_customer_id
from customer_total_return ctr1
join store_avg a on a.ctr_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk
join customer c on c.c_customer_sk = ctr1.ctr_customer_sk
join customer_demographics cd on c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
where ctr1.ctr_total_return > a.avg_ctr_total_return * 1.2
  and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk between 24 and 27
  and cd.cd_marital_status in ('S', 'U')
  and cd.cd_education_status in ('Secondary', '4 yr Degree')
  and cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  and c.c_birth_month = 6
  and c.c_birth_year between 1934 and 1940
order by c.c_customer_id
limit 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated scalar subquery computing AVG(ctr_total_return) per store row with a pre-aggregated store_avg CTE joined on ctr_store_sk, avoiding repeated CTE scans.

Push the store state filter (s_state IN ('IA','NE','TX')) into the CTE by joining store early, reducing the aggregated rows; safe because the average is per-store and only stores in those states can appear in the output.
Rewrite implicit comma joins as explicit JOIN ... ON clauses for clearer join order and better optimizer handling.
Compute the per-store average once via GROUP BY in the store_avg CTE instead of per-row subquery evaluation; multiply by 1.2 at comparison time, preserving original semantics.

original_query: with customer_total_return as (select sr_customer_sk as ctr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk as ctr_store_sk ,sr_reason_sk as ctr_reason_sk ,sum(SR_STORE_CREDIT) as ctr_total_return from store_returns ,date_dim where sr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk and d_year =2000 and sr_return_amt / sr_return_quantity between 107 and 166 group by sr_customer_sk ,sr_store_sk, sr_reason_sk)  select  c_customer_id from customer_total_return ctr1 ,store ,customer ,customer_demographics where ctr1.ctr_total_return > (select avg(ctr_total_return)*1.2 from customer_total_return ctr2 where ctr1.ctr_store_sk = ctr2.ctr_store_sk ) and ctr1.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20 and s_store_sk = ctr1.ctr_store_sk and s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA') and ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c_customer_sk and c_current_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk and cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W') and cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown') and cd_gender = 'F' and c_birth_month = 5 and c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962 order by c_customer_id limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT sr.sr_customer_sk AS ctr_customer_sk,
           sr.sr_store_sk AS ctr_store_sk,
           sr.sr_reason_sk AS ctr_reason_sk,
           SUM(sr.sr_store_credit) AS ctr_total_return
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = sr.sr_store_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2000
      AND sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 107 AND 166
      AND s.s_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA')
    GROUP BY sr.sr_customer_sk, sr.sr_store_sk, sr.sr_reason_sk
),
store_avg AS (
    SELECT ctr_store_sk,
           AVG(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 AS avg_threshold
    FROM customer_total_return
    GROUP BY ctr_store_sk
)
SELECT c.c_customer_id
FROM customer_total_return ctr
JOIN store_avg sa ON ctr.ctr_store_sk = sa.ctr_store_sk
JOIN customer c ON c.c_customer_sk = ctr.ctr_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON c.c_current_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
WHERE ctr.ctr_total_return > sa.avg_threshold
  AND ctr.ctr_reason_sk BETWEEN 17 AND 20
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W')
  AND cd.cd_education_status IN ('College', 'Unknown')
  AND cd.cd_gender = 'F'
  AND c.c_birth_month = 5
  AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1956 AND 1962
ORDER BY c.c_customer_id
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the correlated subquery (per-row AVG over customer_total_return ctr2) with a pre-aggregated store_avg CTE computing AVG(ctr_total_return)*1.2 once per store, then join. This eliminates repeated CTE scans per outer row and improves scalability (score 8/10).

Push the highly selective store filter s_state IN ('MO','NC','PA') into the customer_total_return CTE by joining store before aggregation. Since store state is constant per store_sk, the per-store average is unchanged, while rows scanned/grouped can drop dramatically (store table only 102 rows, ~3/102 states selected) (score 9/10).

Convert implicit comma joins into explicit INNER JOINs. After pushing the store filter into the CTE, the outer store join becomes redundant and is removed; customer and customer_demographics remain as join predicates in the main query.

WITH date_filter AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_year = 1998
      AND d_moy BETWEEN 7 AND 10
),
item_filter AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Children', 'Electronics', 'Home')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 68 AND 77
),
store_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ss.ss_customer_sk AS customer_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_filter d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item_filter i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
),
web_catalog_customers AS (
    SELECT ws.ws_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_filter d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item_filter i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_sales_price / ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
    UNION
    SELECT cs.cs_ship_customer_sk AS customer_sk
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_filter d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item_filter i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_sales_price / cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 0.90 AND 1.00
)
SELECT
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt1,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt2,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt3,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt4,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt5,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count,
    COUNT(*) AS cnt6
FROM customer c
JOIN customer_address ca ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN store_customers sc ON sc.customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN web_catalog_customers wc ON wc.customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
WHERE ca.ca_county IN ('Benton County','Clarke County','La Paz County','Lexington city','Power County')
  AND c.c_birth_month IN (9, 11)
  AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('D', 'W', 'M')

GROUP BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count
ORDER BY
    cd.cd_gender,
    cd.cd_marital_status,
    cd.cd_education_status,
    cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
    cd.cd_credit_rating,
    cd.cd_dep_count,
    cd.cd_dep_employed_count,
    cd.cd_dep_college_count
LIMIT 100;

store_customers AS (

SELECT MIN(ss.ss_quantity),
       MIN(ss.ss_ext_sales_price),
       MIN(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost),
       MIN(ss.ss_ext_wholesale_cost)
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN date_dim d
  ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cd.cd_demo_sk = ss.ss_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = ss.ss_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = ss.ss_addr_sk
WHERE d.d_year = 2001
  AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND (
        (cd.cd_marital_status = 'U'
         AND cd.cd_education_status = 'College'
         AND (
              (ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 100.00 AND 150.00 AND hd.hd_dep_count = 3)
           OR (ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 100.00 AND hd.hd_dep_count = 1)
         ))
     OR (cd.cd_marital_status = 'S'
         AND cd.cd_education_status = 'Secondary'
         AND ss.ss_sales_price BETWEEN 150.00 AND 200.00
         AND hd.hd_dep_count = 1)
      )
  AND (
        (ca.ca_state IN ('AR', 'OK', 'TX') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 200)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('KS', 'MN', 'TX') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 150 AND 300)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('KS', 'MD', 'NV') AND ss.ss_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 250)
      );

Factored the common predicate ca_country = 'United States' out of the three address OR branches, and factored cd_marital_status = 'U' AND cd_education_status = 'College' out of the first two demographic branches, reducing repeated predicate evaluation inside the join filter.

The duplicated MIN(ss_ext_wholesale_cost) is retained to preserve the 4-column output; most optimizers deduplicate identical aggregate expressions, so no subquery wrapper was added to avoid unnecessary restructuring.

Splitting the OR groups into UNION ALL branches was considered. Since MIN is idempotent under duplicates it would be semantically safe, but with store_sales (~28.8M rows) and only a date index, 3 or 9 repeated scans of the date-filtered sales would likely regress; a single-scan factored form is preferred.

WITH
store_base AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_quantity AS quantity,
           ss.ss_list_price AS list_price,
           d.d_week_seq,
           i.i_brand_id,
           i.i_class_id,
           i.i_category_id,
           i.i_category,
           i.i_manager_id
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
catalog_base AS (
    SELECT cs.cs_quantity AS quantity,
           cs.cs_list_price AS list_price,
           i.i_brand_id,
           i.i_class_id,
           i.i_category_id,
           i.i_category,
           i.i_manager_id
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
web_base AS (
    SELECT ws.ws_quantity AS quantity,
           ws.ws_list_price AS list_price,
           i.i_brand_id,
           i.i_class_id,
           i.i_category_id
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
),
cross_keys AS (
    SELECT i_brand_id AS brand_id,
           i_class_id AS class_id,
           i_category_id AS category_id
    FROM store_base
    WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
    INTERSECT
    SELECT i_brand_id,
           i_class_id,
           i_category_id
    FROM catalog_base
    WHERE i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
    INTERSECT
    SELECT i_brand_id,
           i_class_id,
           i_category_id
    FROM web_base
),
avg_sales AS (
    SELECT AVG(quantity * list_price) AS average_sales
    FROM (
        SELECT quantity, list_price FROM store_base
        UNION ALL
        SELECT quantity, list_price FROM catalog_base
        UNION ALL
        SELECT quantity, list_price FROM web_base
    ) x
),
date_weeks AS (
    SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 5 THEN d_week_seq END) AS this_week_seq,
           MAX(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 5 THEN d_week_seq END) AS last_week_seq
    FROM date_dim
),
agg AS (
    SELECT sb.i_brand_id,
           sb.i_class_id,
           sb.i_category_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN sb.d_week_seq = w.this_week_seq THEN sb.quantity * sb.list_price END) AS ty_sales,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN sb.d_week_seq = w.this_week_seq THEN 1 END) AS ty_number_sales,
           SUM(CASE WHEN sb.d_week_seq = w.last_week_seq THEN sb.quantity * sb.list_price END) AS ly_sales,
           COUNT(CASE WHEN sb.d_week_seq = w.last_week_seq THEN 1 END) AS ly_number_sales
    FROM store_base sb
    JOIN cross_keys ck
      ON sb.i_brand_id = ck.brand_id
     AND sb.i_class_id = ck.class_id
     AND sb.i_category_id = ck.category_id
    CROSS JOIN date_weeks w
    WHERE sb.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND sb.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 37
      AND sb.d_week_seq IN (w.this_week_seq, w.last_week_seq)
    GROUP BY sb.i_brand_id, sb.i_class_id, sb.i_category_id
)
SELECT 'store' AS ty_channel,
       a.i_brand_id AS ty_brand,
       a.i_class_id AS ty_class,
       a.i_category_id AS ty_category,
       a.ty_sales,
       a.ty_number_sales,
       'store' AS ly_channel,
       a.i_brand_id AS ly_brand,
       a.i_class_id AS ly_class,
       a.i_category_id AS ly_category,
       a.ly_sales,
       a.ly_number_sales
FROM agg a
CROSS JOIN avg_sales av
WHERE a.ty_sales > av.average_sales
  AND a.ly_sales > av.average_sales
ORDER BY ty_channel, ty_brand, ty_class, ty_category
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Consolidate repeated scans of store_sales, catalog_sales and web_sales: each large fact table is scanned twice (once for cross_items, once for avg_sales) plus an extra scan of store_sales for the final aggregation. Materialize each filtered fact table once in a base CTE (year 1998-2000, wholesale_cost 80-100, joined to item/date_dim) and reuse it across cross_keys, avg_sales and the final aggregation.

Replace the materialized item_sk list (cross_items) with an intersection of distinct (brand, class, category) keys (cross_keys), then join the final aggregation directly on those keys. This removes an extra item lookup and the IN subquery while preserving semantics since the outer item filters (category, manager) are applied in the final aggregation.

Merge the two nearly identical this_year / last_year store_sales aggregations into a single scan with conditional aggregation (SUM/COUNT CASE on d_week_seq), replacing the costly self-join between two aggregate subqueries.

Convert all comma-style joins into explicit INNER JOIN syntax to avoid accidental Cartesian products and improve readability; keep the web branch of cross_keys free of category/manager filters to match the original semantics.
Fold the expressions 1998 + 2 -> 2000 and 1998 + 1 -> 1999 at rewrite time.

Collapse the two scalar d_week_seq subqueries into a single date_weeks CTE computing both week sequences in one pass over date_dim; the redundant i_category/i_manager_id filters that appeared both in cross_items and the outer query are retained only where they are semantically needed (cross_keys store/catalog branches and final aggregation).

with cross_items as (
  select sc.brand_id, sc.class_id, sc.category_id, i.i_item_sk
  from item i
  join (
    select i_brand_id brand_id, i_class_id class_id, i_category_id category_id
    from (
      select iss.i_brand_id, iss.i_class_id, iss.i_category_id
      from store_sales ss
      join item iss on ss.ss_item_sk = iss.i_item_sk
      join date_dim d1 on ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
      where d1.d_year between 1998 and 2000
        and iss.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
        and iss.i_manager_id between 14 and 23
        and ss.ss_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
      intersect
      select ics.i_brand_id, ics.i_class_id, ics.i_category_id
      from catalog_sales cs
      join item ics on cs.cs_item_sk = ics.i_item_sk
      join date_dim d2 on cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
      where d2.d_year between 1998 and 2000
        and ics.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
        and ics.i_manager_id between 14 and 23
        and cs.cs_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
    ) st_ca
    where exists (
      select 1
      from web_sales ws
      join item iws on ws.ws_item_sk = iws.i_item_sk
      join date_dim d3 on ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
      where iws.i_brand_id = st_ca.i_brand_id
        and iws.i_class_id = st_ca.i_class_id
        and iws.i_category_id = st_ca.i_category_id
        and ws.ws_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
        and d3.d_year between 1998 and 2000
    )
  ) sc on i.i_brand_id = sc.brand_id
      and i.i_class_id = sc.class_id
      and i.i_category_id = sc.category_id
  where i.i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
    and i.i_manager_id between 14 and 23
),
avg_sales as (
  select avg(quantity * list_price) average_sales
  from (
    select ss_quantity quantity, ss_list_price list_price
    from store_sales join date_dim on ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
    where d_year between 1998 and 2000 and ss_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
    union all
    select cs_quantity, cs_list_price
    from catalog_sales join date_dim on cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
    where d_year between 1998 and 2000 and cs_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
    union all
    select ws_quantity, ws_list_price
    from web_sales join date_dim on ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
    where d_year between 1998 and 2000 and ws_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
  ) x
)
select
  ty.channel ty_channel,
  ty.i_brand_id ty_brand, ty.i_class_id ty_class, ty.i_category_id ty_category,
  ty.sales ty_sales, ty.number_sales ty_number_sales,
  ly.channel ly_channel,
  ly.i_brand_id ly_brand, ly.i_class_id ly_class, ly.i_category_id ly_category,
  ly.sales ly_sales, ly.number_sales ly_number_sales
from (
  select 'store' channel, i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id,
         sum(ss_quantity * ss_list_price) sales, count(*) number_sales
  from store_sales
  join item on ss_item_sk = i_item_sk
  join date_dim on ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
  where ss_item_sk in (select ss_item_sk from cross_items)
    and d_week_seq = (select d_week_seq from date_dim where d_year = 1999 and d_moy = 12 and d_dom = 13)
    and i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
    and i_manager_id between 14 and 23
    and ss_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
  group by i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id
  having sum(ss_quantity * ss_list_price) > (select average_sales from avg_sales)
) ty
join (
  select 'store' channel, i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id,
         sum(ss_quantity * ss_list_price) sales, count(*) number_sales
  from store_sales
  join item on ss_item_sk = i_item_sk
  join date_dim on ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk
  where ss_item_sk in (select ss_item_sk from cross_items)
    and d_week_seq = (select d_week_seq from date_dim where d_year = 1998 and d_moy = 12 and d_dom = 13)
    and i_category in ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
    and i_manager_id between 14 and 23
    and ss_wholesale_cost between 78 and 98
  group by i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id
  having sum(ss_quantity * ss_list_price) > (select average_sales from avg_sales)
) ly
  on ty.i_brand_id = ly.i_brand_id

rewritten_query:
WITH store_brands AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Men', 'Women')
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 49 AND 58
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
),
catalog_brands AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Men', 'Women')
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 49 AND 58
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
),
web_brands AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
),
cross_brands AS (
    SELECT sb.i_brand_id, sb.i_class_id, sb.i_category_id
    FROM store_brands sb
    JOIN catalog_brands cb
      ON sb.i_brand_id = cb.i_brand_id
     AND sb.i_class_id = cb.i_class_id
     AND sb.i_category_id = cb.i_category_id
    JOIN web_brands wb
      ON sb.i_brand_id = wb.i_brand_id
     AND sb.i_class_id = wb.i_class_id
     AND sb.i_category_id = wb.i_category_id
),
avg_sales AS (
    SELECT SUM(sales_amt) / SUM(row_cnt) AS average_sales
    FROM (
        SELECT SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) AS sales_amt,
               COUNT(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) AS row_cnt
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        UNION ALL
        SELECT SUM(cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price),
               COUNT(cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price)
        FROM catalog_sales cs
        JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
        UNION ALL
        SELECT SUM(ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price),
               COUNT(ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price)
        FROM web_sales ws
        JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year BETWEEN 1998 AND 2000
          AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
    ) x
),
target_weeks AS (
    SELECT MAX(d_week_seq) FILTER (WHERE d_year = 1999 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 9) AS week_1999,
           MAX(d_week_seq) FILTER (WHERE d_year = 1998 AND d_moy = 12 AND d_dom = 9) AS week_1998
    FROM date_dim
),
store_agg AS (
    SELECT
        i.i_brand_id,
        i.i_class_id,
        i.i_category_id,
        SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1999) AS ty_sales,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1999) AS ty_number_sales,
        SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1998) AS ly_sales,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1998) AS ly_number_sales
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN cross_brands cb
      ON i.i_brand_id = cb.i_brand_id
     AND i.i_class_id = cb.i_class_id
     AND i.i_category_id = cb.i_category_id
    CROSS JOIN target_weeks tw
    CROSS JOIN avg_sales av
    WHERE d.d_week_seq IN (tw.week_1999, tw.week_1998)
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Men', 'Women')
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 49 AND 58
      AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 23 AND 43
    GROUP BY i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id, tw.week_1999, tw.week_1998, av.average_sales
    HAVING
        SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1999) > av.average_sales
        AND SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_list_price) FILTER (WHERE d.d_week_seq = tw.week_1998) > av.average_sales
)
SELECT
    'store' AS ty_channel,
    i_brand_id AS ty_brand,
    i_class_id AS ty_class,
    i_category_id AS ty_category,
    ty_sales,
    ty_number_sales,
    'store' AS ly_channel,
    i_brand_id AS ly_brand,
    i_class_id AS ly_class,
    i_category_id AS ly_category,
    ly_sales,
    ly_number_sales
FROM store_agg
ORDER BY ty_channel, ty_brand, ty_class, ty_category
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the item-level cross_items CTE (INTERSECT + join back to item producing item_sk) with a brand/class/category level intersection (cross_brands). Since the main query already joins item and filters i_category/i_manager_id and groups by brand/class/category, filtering directly on cross_brands is equivalent and eliminates an expensive redundant CTE join.

Merge the separate this_year and last_year subqueries into a single aggregation over store_sales using conditional aggregation (FILTER on the two target d_week_seq values), avoiding two scans of store_sales/item/date_dim and replacing the final self-join on brand/class/category.

Replace nested INTERSECT set operations with per-channel DISTINCT CTEs (store_brands, catalog_brands, web_brands) joined together, enabling hash joins instead of repeated set-operator sorts. Use explicit JOIN syntax throughout.

Rewrite avg_sales as per-channel SUM/COUNT aggregates combined into a global average (SUM(sales_amt)/SUM(row_cnt)), reducing input to the final aggregation; the CTE is materialized once and cross-joined into the HAVING clause instead of repeated scalar subqueries.
Fold 1998 + 2 into 2000 and 1998 + 1 into 1999, and compute the two target week_seq values once in a target_weeks CTE instead of repeated correlated scalar subqueries.

    FROM item
    WHERE i_category = 'Home'
),
filtered_customer AS (

           LEFT(ca.ca_zip, 5) AS ca_zip5
    FROM customer c

      ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk

),

)
SELECT
    i.i_brand_id AS brand_id,
    i.i_brand AS brand,

ORDER BY ext_price DESC,

WITH frequent_ss_items AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ss.ss_item_sk AS item_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 12 AND 31
      AND i.i_category IN ('Children', 'Home', 'Women')
    GROUP BY ss.ss_item_sk, ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 4
),
max_store_sales AS (
    SELECT MAX(csales) AS tpcds_cmax
    FROM (
        SELECT ss.ss_customer_sk AS c_customer_sk,
               SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) AS csales
        FROM store_sales ss
        JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
        JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year = 2001
          AND ss.ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
        GROUP BY ss.ss_customer_sk
    ) tmp1
),
candidate_sales AS (
    SELECT cs.cs_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           cs.cs_quantity * cs.cs_list_price AS sales
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 7
      AND cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frequent_ss_items f WHERE f.item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT ws.ws_bill_customer_sk AS customer_sk,
           ws.ws_quantity * ws.ws_list_price AS sales
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND d.d_moy = 7
      AND ws.ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 30 AND 40
      AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM frequent_ss_items f WHERE f.item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk)
),
candidate_customers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT customer_sk
    FROM candidate_sales
    WHERE customer_sk IS NOT NULL
),
qualified_customers AS (
    SELECT ss.ss_customer_sk AS c_customer_sk
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    JOIN candidate_customers cc ON cc.customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
    WHERE c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1940 AND 1946
    GROUP BY ss.ss_customer_sk
    HAVING SUM(ss.ss_quantity * ss.ss_sales_price) > 0.95 * (SELECT tpcds_cmax FROM max_store_sales)
)
SELECT SUM(cs.sales)
FROM candidate_sales cs
WHERE EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM qualified_customers qc
    WHERE qc.c_customer_sk = cs.customer_sk
)
LIMIT 100;

Simplify frequent_ss_items: remove the unused substring(i_item_desc,1,30) (functionally dependent on i_item_sk PK) and group by ss_item_sk, ss_sold_date_sk (equivalent to d_date since d_date_sk is unique per date). SELECT i.i_item_id,
       i.i_item_desc,
       s.s_store_id,
       s.s_store_name,
       SUM(ss.ss_net_profit) AS store_sales_profit,
       SUM(sr.sr_net_loss)  AS store_returns_loss,
       SUM(cs.cs_net_profit) AS catalog_sales_profit
FROM store_sales ss
JOIN store_returns sr
  ON sr.sr_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
 AND sr.sr_item_sk     = ss.ss_item_sk
 AND sr.sr_ticket_number = ss.ss_ticket_number
JOIN catalog_sales cs
  ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
 AND cs.cs_item_sk          = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON d1.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON d2.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
JOIN date_dim d3
  ON d3.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
JOIN store s
  ON s.s_store_sk = ss.ss_store_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
WHERE d1.d_moy  = 8
  AND d1.d_year = 2001
  AND d2.d_moy  BETWEEN 8 AND 10
  AND d2.d_year = 2001
  AND d3.d_moy  BETWEEN 8 AND 10
  AND d3.d_year = 2001
GROUP BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
ORDER BY i.i_item_id, i.i_item_desc, s.s_store_id, s.s_store_name
LIMIT 100;

Keep the fact-table join order (store_sales -> store_returns -> catalog_sales) with join keys in ON clauses; keep date_dim/store/item as inline dimension joins rather than a shared CTE for d2/d3, since the previous CTE-based plan cost 42,546 vs 35,795 (the materialized CTE lost index access on d_date_sk).     FROM web_returns wr
    JOIN date_dim d ON wr.wr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN customer_address ca ON wr.wr_returning_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
    JOIN item i ON wr.wr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 2001
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 69 AND 78

        ca.ca_state,
        wr.wr_reason_sk
)
SELECT

    c.c_first_name,

    c.c_birth_country,
    c.c_login,

    from web_returns wr
    join date_dim d on wr.wr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    join customer_address ra on wr.wr_returning_addr_sk = ra.ca_address_sk
    join item i on wr.wr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk

),
state_avg as (
    select ctr_state

WITH monthly_stats AS (
    SELECT w_warehouse_sk,
           i_item_sk,
           d_moy,
           stdev,
           mean,
           stdev / mean AS cov
    FROM (
        SELECT w.w_warehouse_sk AS w_warehouse_sk,
               inv.inv_item_sk AS i_item_sk,
               d.d_moy,
               stddev_samp(inv.inv_quantity_on_hand) AS stdev,
               avg(inv.inv_quantity_on_hand) AS mean
        FROM inventory inv
        JOIN item i ON inv.inv_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
        JOIN warehouse w ON inv.inv_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
        JOIN date_dim d ON inv.inv_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
        WHERE d.d_year = 1998
          AND d.d_moy IN (2, 3)
          AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home')
          AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 47
          AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand BETWEEN 225 AND 425
        GROUP BY w.w_warehouse_sk, inv.inv_item_sk, d.d_moy
    ) s
    WHERE stdev > mean
)
SELECT inv1.w_warehouse_sk,
       inv1.i_item_sk,
       inv1.d_moy,
       inv1.mean,
       inv1.cov,
       inv2.w_warehouse_sk,
       inv2.i_item_sk,
       inv2.d_moy,
       inv2.mean,
       inv2.cov
FROM monthly_stats inv1
JOIN monthly_stats inv2
  ON inv1.i_item_sk = inv2.i_item_sk
 AND inv1.w_warehouse_sk = inv2.w_warehouse_sk
WHERE inv1.d_moy = 2
  AND inv2.d_moy = 3
ORDER BY inv1.w_warehouse_sk,

original_query: select     s_store_name   ,s_company_id   ,s_street_number   ,s_street_name   ,s_street_type   ,s_suite_number   ,s_city   ,s_county   ,s_state   ,s_zip   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 30 ) then 1 else 0 end)  as "30 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 30) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 60) then 1 else 0 end )  as "31-60 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 60) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 90) then 1 else 0 end)  as "61-90 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk > 90) and                  (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk <= 120) then 1 else 0 end)  as "91-120 days"   ,sum(case when (sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk  > 120) then 1 else 0 end)  as ">120 days" from    store_sales   ,store_returns   ,store   ,date_dim d1   ,date_dim d2 where     d2.d_year = 2000 and d2.d_moy  = 4 and ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number and ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk and ss_sold_date_sk   = d1.d_date_sk and sr_returned_date_sk   = d2.d_date_sk and ss_customer_sk = sr_customer_sk and ss_store_sk = s_store_sk and d1.d_date between (d2.d_date - interval '120' day)                and d2.d_date group by    s_store_name   ,s_company_id   ,s_street_number   ,s_street_name   ,s_street_type   ,s_suite_number   ,s_city   ,s_county   ,s_state   ,s_zip order by s_store_name         ,s_company_id         ,s_street_number         ,s_street_name         ,s_street_type         ,s_suite_number         ,s_city         ,s_county         ,s_state         ,s_zip limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH filtered_returns AS (
    SELECT
        sr.sr_ticket_number,
        sr.sr_item_sk,
        sr.sr_customer_sk,
        sr.sr_returned_date_sk,
        d2.d_date AS return_date
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN date_dim d2
      ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
    WHERE d2.d_date >= DATE '2000-04-01'
      AND d2.d_date <  DATE '2000-05-01'
),
return_days AS (
    SELECT
        ss.ss_store_sk,
        sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk AS days_between
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN filtered_returns sr
      ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
     AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
    JOIN date_dim d1
      ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
    WHERE d1.d_date >= sr.return_date - INTERVAL '120 days'
      AND d1.d_date <= sr.return_date
      AND d1.d_date >= DATE '1999-12-03'
      AND d1.d_date <= DATE '2000-04-30'
),
store_agg AS (
    SELECT
        ss_store_sk,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_between <= 30) AS "30 days",
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_between > 30 AND days_between <= 60) AS "31-60 days",
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_between > 60 AND days_between <= 90) AS "61-90 days",
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_between > 90 AND days_between <= 120) AS "91-120 days",
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_between > 120) AS ">120 days"
    FROM return_days
    GROUP BY ss_store_sk
)
SELECT
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip,
    a."30 days",
    a."31-60 days",
    a."61-90 days",
    a."91-120 days",
    a.">120 days"
FROM store_agg a
JOIN store s
  ON a.ss_store_sk = s.s_store_sk
ORDER BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
LIMIT 100;

with store_agg as (
    select ss.ss_store_sk,
           sum(case when sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk <= 30 then 1 else 0 end) as "30 days",
           sum(case when sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk between 31 and 60 then 1 else 0 end) as "31-60 days",
           sum(case when sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk between 61 and 90 then 1 else 0 end) as "61-90 days",
           sum(case when sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk between 91 and 120 then 1 else 0 end) as "91-120 days",

    from store_sales ss

),

    join item i on i.i_item_sk = s.item_sk
    join date_dim d on d.d_date_sk = s.sold_date_sk
    where i.i_category = 'Electronics'
      and i.i_class = 'portable'
      and d.d_year = 2002
      and d.d_moy = 6
      and s.wholesale_cost between 70 and 100
),
my_customers as (
    select c.c_customer_sk, c.c_current_addr_sk
    from customer c
    join qualifying_customers qc on qc.customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    where c.c_birth_year between 1978 and 1991
),
my_revenue as (
    select c.c_customer_sk,
           sum(ss.ss_ext_sales_price) as revenue
    from my_customers c
    join store_sales ss on ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    join customer_address ca on ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
    join store s on s.s_county = ca.ca_county and s.s_state = ca.ca_state
    join date_dim d on d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    where ss.ss_wholesale_cost between 70 and 100

      and ca.ca_state in ('AL','AR','FL','MN','MO','NC','NY','OK','PA','WI')
      and d.d_year = 2002

),
segments as (

    from my_revenue

from segments
group by segment
order by segment, num_customers
limit 100;

WITH params AS (

    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq = (
        SELECT d_month_seq
        FROM date_dim
        WHERE d_date = DATE '1999-02-11'
    )
),
ss_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ss.ss_ext_sales_price) AS ss_item_rev
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN params p ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ss.ss_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
cs_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,

    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN params p ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON cs.cs_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON cs.cs_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
ws_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           c.c_birth_year AS birth_year,
           SUM(ws.ws_ext_sales_price) AS ws_item_rev
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN params p ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = p.d_date_sk
    JOIN item i ON ws.ws_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    JOIN customer c ON ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 269 AND 298
      AND i.i_manager_id BETWEEN 28 AND 57
      AND c.c_birth_year BETWEEN 1938 AND 1944
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id, c.c_birth_year
),
combined AS (
    SELECT ss.item_id,
           ss.birth_year,
           ss.ss_item_rev,
           cs.cs_item_rev,
           ws.ws_item_rev,
           (ss.ss_item_rev + cs.cs_item_rev + ws.ws_item_rev) / 3.0 AS avg_rev
    FROM ss_items ss
    JOIN cs_items cs
      ON ss.item_id = cs.item_id
     AND ss.birth_year = cs.birth_year
    JOIN ws_items ws
      ON ss.item_id = ws.item_id
     AND ss.birth_year = ws.birth_year
    WHERE ss.ss_item_rev * 11 >= cs.cs_item_rev * 10
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 10 <= cs.cs_item_rev * 11
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 11 >= ws.ws_item_rev * 10
      AND ss.ss_item_rev * 10 <= ws.ws_item_rev * 11
      AND cs.cs_item_rev * 11 >= ws.ws_item_rev * 10
      AND cs.cs_item_rev * 10 <= ws.ws_item_rev * 11
)

       ws_item_rev,
       ws_item_rev / avg_rev * 100 AS ws_dev,
       avg_rev AS average
FROM combined

LIMIT 100;

The store state filter (s_state IN ...) was applied twice after aggregation in the y and x subqueries. It is pushed into the `wss` CTE before aggregation, reducing the number of stores aggregated (~26% reduction) and making the outer s_state filters redundant.

Implicit comma joins were rewritten to explicit ANSI JOINs. The date_dim joins in y/x are preserved because they control row multiplication semantics (one row per day in each week within the month range) and must not be removed to keep the result equivalent.
Constants such as 17*0.01 and 37*0.01 and month boundaries (1207+11, 1207+12, 1207+23) are trivially folded by the optimizer; the BETWEEN date-month bounds are kept as-is for clarity.

    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq BETWEEN 1210 AND 1233

    WHERE cd1.cd_marital_status <> cd2.cd_marital_status

original_query: select    cd_gender,   cd_marital_status,   cd_education_status,   count(*) cnt1,   cd_purchase_estimate,   count(*) cnt2,   cd_credit_rating,   count(*) cnt3  from   customer c,customer_address ca,customer_demographics  where   c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk and   ca_state in ('MD','MO','OK') and   cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk   and cd_marital_status in ('W', 'U', 'W')   and cd_education_status in ('Primary', 'Primary') and   exists (select *           from store_sales,date_dim           where c.c_customer_sk = ss_customer_sk and                 ss_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                 d_year = 2002 and                 d_moy between 5 and 5+2                 and ss_list_price between 132 and 221           ) and    (not exists (select *             from web_sales,date_dim             where c.c_customer_sk = ws_bill_customer_sk and                   ws_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                   d_year = 2002 and                   d_moy between 5 and 5+2                   and ws_list_price between 132 and 221             ) and     not exists (select *             from catalog_sales,date_dim             where c.c_customer_sk = cs_ship_customer_sk and                   cs_sold_date_sk = d_date_sk and                   d_year = 2002 and                   d_moy between 5 and 5+2                   and cs_list_price between 132 and 221)             )  group by cd_gender,           cd_marital_status,           cd_education_status,           cd_purchase_estimate,           cd_credit_rating  order by cd_gender,           cd_marital_status,           cd_education_status,           cd_purchase_estimate,           cd_credit_rating  limit 100;
rewritten_query:
SELECT
    t.cd_gender,
    t.cd_marital_status,
    t.cd_education_status,
    t.cnt AS cnt1,
    t.cd_purchase_estimate,
    t.cnt AS cnt2,
    t.cd_credit_rating,
    t.cnt AS cnt3
FROM (
    SELECT
        cd.cd_gender,
        cd.cd_marital_status,
        cd.cd_education_status,
        cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
        cd.cd_credit_rating,
        COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM customer c
    JOIN customer_address ca
      ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
    JOIN customer_demographics cd
      ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
    WHERE ca.ca_state IN ('MD', 'MO', 'OK')
      AND cd.cd_marital_status IN ('W', 'U')
      AND cd.cd_education_status = 'Primary'
      AND EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM store_sales ss
          JOIN date_dim d ON ss.ss_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
          WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
            AND d.d_year = 2002
            AND d.d_moy BETWEEN 5 AND 7
            AND ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 132 AND 221
      )
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM web_sales ws
          JOIN date_dim d ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
          WHERE ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
            AND d.d_year = 2002
            AND d.d_moy BETWEEN 5 AND 7
            AND ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 132 AND 221
      )
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM catalog_sales cs
          JOIN date_dim d ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
          WHERE cs.cs_ship_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
            AND d.d_year = 2002
            AND d.d_moy BETWEEN 5 AND 7
            AND cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 132 AND 221
      )
    GROUP BY
        cd.cd_gender,
        cd.cd_marital_status,
        cd.cd_education_status,
        cd.cd_purchase_estimate,
        cd.cd_credit_rating
) t
ORDER BY
    t.cd_gender,
    t.cd_marital_status,
    t.cd_education_status,
    t.cd_purchase_estimate,
    t.cd_credit_rating
LIMIT 100;

original_query: select  i_item_desc       ,w_warehouse_name       ,d1.d_week_seq       ,sum(case when p_promo_sk is null then 1 else 0 end) no_promo       ,sum(case when p_promo_sk is not null then 1 else 0 end) promo       ,count(*) total_cnt from catalog_sales join inventory on (cs_item_sk = inv_item_sk) join warehouse on (w_warehouse_sk=inv_warehouse_sk) join item on (i_item_sk = cs_item_sk) join customer_demographics on (cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd_demo_sk) join household_demographics on (cs_bill_hdemo_sk = hd_demo_sk) join date_dim d1 on (cs_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk) join date_dim d2 on (inv_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk) join date_dim d3 on (cs_ship_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk) left outer join promotion on (cs_promo_sk=p_promo_sk) left outer join catalog_returns on (cr_item_sk = cs_item_sk and cr_order_number = cs_order_number) where d1.d_week_seq = d2.d_week_seq   and inv_quantity_on_hand < cs_quantity   and d3.d_date > d1.d_date + interval '3 day'   and hd_buy_potential = '1001-5000'   and d1.d_year = 2001   and cd_marital_status = 'U'   and cd_dep_count between 5 and 7   and i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')   and cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100 group by i_item_desc,w_warehouse_name,d1.d_week_seq order by total_cnt desc, i_item_desc, w_warehouse_name, d_week_seq limit 100;

SELECT
    i.i_item_desc,
    w.w_warehouse_name,
    d1.d_week_seq,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cs.cs_promo_sk IS NULL) AS no_promo,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE cs.cs_promo_sk IS NOT NULL) AS promo,
    COUNT(*) AS total_cnt
FROM catalog_sales cs
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON cs.cs_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk
 AND d1.d_year = 2001
JOIN inventory inv
  ON cs.cs_item_sk = inv.inv_item_sk
JOIN date_dim d2
  ON inv.inv_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
 AND d2.d_week_seq = d1.d_week_seq
JOIN warehouse w
  ON w.w_warehouse_sk = inv.inv_warehouse_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
 AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Home', 'Sports')
JOIN customer_demographics cd
  ON cs.cs_bill_cdemo_sk = cd.cd_demo_sk
 AND cd.cd_marital_status = 'U'
 AND cd.cd_dep_count BETWEEN 5 AND 7
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON cs.cs_bill_hdemo_sk = hd.hd_demo_sk
 AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '1001-5000'
JOIN date_dim d3
  ON cs.cs_ship_date_sk = d3.d_date_sk
 AND d3.d_date > d1.d_date + INTERVAL '3 day'
WHERE cs.cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 80 AND 100
  AND inv.inv_quantity_on_hand < cs.cs_quantity
GROUP BY i.i_item_desc, w.w_warehouse_name, d1.d_week_seq

WITH sales_detail AS (
    SELECT
        d_year,
        i_brand_id,
        i_class_id,
        i_category_id,
        i_manufact_id,
        cs_quantity - COALESCE(cr_return_quantity, 0) AS sales_cnt,
        cs_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(cr_return_amount, 0.0) AS sales_amt
    FROM catalog_sales
    JOIN item ON i_item_sk = cs_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim ON d_date_sk = cs_sold_date_sk
    LEFT JOIN catalog_returns
           ON cs_order_number = cr_order_number
          AND cs_item_sk = cr_item_sk
    WHERE i_category = 'Sports'
      AND d_year IN (1998, 1999)
      AND cs_sales_price / cs_list_price BETWEEN 0.80 AND 1.00
      AND cr_reason_sk IN (7, 10, 12, 29, 45)

    UNION

    SELECT
        d_year,
        i_brand_id,
        i_class_id,
        i_category_id,
        i_manufact_id,
        ss_quantity - COALESCE(sr_return_quantity, 0),
        ss_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(sr_return_amt, 0.0)
    FROM store_sales
    JOIN item ON i_item_sk = ss_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim ON d_date_sk = ss_sold_date_sk
    LEFT JOIN store_returns
           ON ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number
          AND ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk
    WHERE i_category = 'Sports'
      AND d_year IN (1998, 1999)
      AND ss_sales_price / ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.80 AND 1.00
      AND sr_reason_sk IN (7, 10, 12, 29, 45)

    UNION

    SELECT
        d_year,
        i_brand_id,
        i_class_id,
        i_category_id,
        i_manufact_id,
        ws_quantity - COALESCE(wr_return_quantity, 0),
        ws_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(wr_return_amt, 0.0)
    FROM web_sales
    JOIN item ON i_item_sk = ws_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim ON d_date_sk = ws_sold_date_sk
    LEFT JOIN web_returns
           ON ws_order_number = wr_order_number
          AND ws_item_sk = wr_item_sk
    WHERE i_category = 'Sports'
      AND d_year IN (1998, 1999)
      AND ws_sales_price / ws_list_price BETWEEN 0.80 AND 1.00
      AND wr_reason_sk IN (7, 10, 12, 29, 45)
),
agg AS (
    SELECT
        i_brand_id,
        i_class_id,
        i_category_id,
        i_manufact_id,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 THEN sales_cnt END) AS curr_cnt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 THEN sales_cnt END) AS prev_cnt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 THEN sales_amt END) AS curr_amt,
        SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 THEN sales_amt END) AS prev_amt
    FROM sales_detail
    GROUP BY i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id
)
SELECT
    1998 AS prev_year,
    1999 AS year,
    i_brand_id,
    i_class_id,
    i_category_id,
    i_manufact_id,
    prev_cnt AS prev_yr_cnt,
    curr_cnt AS curr_yr_cnt,
    curr_cnt - prev_cnt AS sales_cnt_diff,
    curr_amt - prev_amt AS sales_amt_diff
FROM agg
WHERE prev_cnt > 0
  AND CAST(curr_cnt AS DECIMAL(17,2)) / CAST(prev_cnt AS DECIMAL(17,2)) < 0.9
ORDER BY sales_cnt_diff, sales_amt_diff
LIMIT 100;

WITH all_sales AS (
  SELECT d_year, i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id,
         SUM(sales_cnt) AS sales_cnt,
         SUM(sales_amt) AS sales_amt
  FROM (
    SELECT d.d_year AS d_year, i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id, i.i_manufact_id,
           cs.cs_quantity - COALESCE(cr.cr_return_quantity,0) AS sales_cnt,
           cs.cs_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(cr.cr_return_amount,0.0) AS sales_amt
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = cs.cs_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = cs.cs_sold_date_sk
    JOIN catalog_returns cr
      ON cs.cs_order_number = cr.cr_order_number AND cs.cs_item_sk = cr.cr_item_sk
     AND cr.cr_reason_sk IN (9,19,23,33,44)
    WHERE i.i_category='Women'
      AND d.d_year IN (2001,2002)
      AND cs.cs_sales_price / cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 68*0.01 AND 88*0.01
    UNION
    SELECT d.d_year, i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id, i.i_manufact_id,
           ss.ss_quantity - COALESCE(sr.sr_return_quantity,0),
           ss.ss_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(sr.sr_return_amt,0.0)
    FROM store_sales ss
    JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = ss.ss_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ss.ss_sold_date_sk
    JOIN store_returns sr
      ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
     AND sr.sr_reason_sk IN (9,19,23,33,44)
    WHERE i.i_category='Women'
      AND d.d_year IN (2001,2002)
      AND ss.ss_sales_price / ss.ss_list_price BETWEEN 68*0.01 AND 88*0.01
    UNION
    SELECT d.d_year, i.i_brand_id, i.i_class_id, i.i_category_id, i.i_manufact_id,
           ws.ws_quantity - COALESCE(wr.wr_return_quantity,0),
           ws.ws_ext_sales_price - COALESCE(wr.wr_return_amt,0.0)
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN item i ON i.i_item_sk = ws.ws_item_sk
    JOIN date_dim d ON d.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
    JOIN web_returns wr
      ON ws.ws_order_number = wr.wr_order_number AND ws.ws_item_sk = wr.wr_item_sk
     AND wr.wr_reason_sk IN (9,19,23,33,44)
    WHERE i.i_category='Women'
      AND d.d_year IN (2001,2002)
      AND ws.ws_sales_price / ws.ws_list_price BETWEEN 68*0.01 AND 88*0.01
  ) sales_detail
  GROUP BY d_year, i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id
),
pivoted AS (
  SELECT i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 2001 THEN sales_cnt END) AS prev_yr_cnt,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 2002 THEN sales_cnt END) AS curr_yr_cnt,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 2001 THEN sales_amt END) AS prev_yr_amt,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 2002 THEN sales_amt END) AS curr_yr_amt
  FROM all_sales
  GROUP BY i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id
)
SELECT 2001 AS prev_year,
       2002 AS year,
       i_brand_id,
       i_class_id,
       i_category_id,
       i_manufact_id,
       prev_yr_cnt,
       curr_yr_cnt,
       curr_yr_cnt - prev_yr_cnt AS sales_cnt_diff,
       curr_yr_amt - prev_yr_amt AS sales_amt_diff
FROM pivoted
WHERE prev_yr_cnt > 0

           SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 THEN sales_cnt END) AS prev_yr_cnt,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 THEN sales_cnt END) AS curr_yr_cnt,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1998 THEN sales_amt END) AS prev_yr_amt,
           SUM(CASE WHEN d_year = 1999 THEN sales_amt END) AS curr_yr_amt
    FROM sales_detail
    GROUP BY i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id
)
SELECT 1998 AS prev_year, 1999 AS year,
       i_brand_id, i_class_id, i_category_id, i_manufact_id,
       prev_yr_cnt, curr_yr_cnt,
       curr_yr_cnt - prev_yr_cnt AS sales_cnt_diff,
       curr_yr_amt - prev_yr_amt AS sales_amt_diff
FROM agg
WHERE prev_yr_cnt > 0
  AND CAST(curr_yr_cnt AS DECIMAL(17,2)) / CAST(prev_yr_cnt AS DECIMAL(17,2)) < 0.9
ORDER BY sales_cnt_diff, sales_amt_diff
LIMIT 100;

Convert LEFT JOIN + WHERE reason_sk IN (...) into an explicit INNER JOIN, since the null-rejecting WHERE predicate on the returned table already makes it an inner join. This clarifies intent and helps the planner. (Score: 6/10)

Fold prev_yr.d_year = 1999-1 into 1998 and inline the constant years into the final SELECT; avoid recomputing 77*0.01 / 97*0.01 by keeping them as-is (already folded by the optimizer). (Score: 3/10)

WITH date_filter AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_date BETWEEN DATE '2001-08-11' AND DATE '2001-09-10'
),
ssr AS (
    SELECT s_store_id AS store_id,
           SUM(ss_ext_sales_price) AS sales,
           SUM(COALESCE(sr_return_amt, 0)) AS returns,
           SUM(ss_net_profit - COALESCE(sr_net_loss, 0)) AS profit
    FROM store_sales
    INNER JOIN date_filter ON ss_sold_date_sk = date_filter.d_date_sk
    INNER JOIN store ON ss_store_sk = s_store_sk
    INNER JOIN item ON ss_item_sk = i_item_sk
    INNER JOIN promotion ON ss_promo_sk = p_promo_sk
    LEFT JOIN store_returns
           ON ss_item_sk = sr_item_sk AND ss_ticket_number = sr_ticket_number
    WHERE i_current_price > 50
      AND p_channel_email = 'N'
      AND p_channel_tv = 'N'
      AND p_channel_radio = 'Y'
      AND p_channel_press = 'N'
      AND p_channel_event = 'Y'
      AND ss_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 45 AND 60
      AND i_category IN ('Jewelry', 'Sports')
    GROUP BY s_store_id
),
csr AS (
    SELECT cp_catalog_page_id AS catalog_page_id,
           SUM(cs_ext_sales_price) AS sales,
           SUM(COALESCE(cr_return_amount, 0)) AS returns,
           SUM(cs_net_profit - COALESCE(cr_net_loss, 0)) AS profit
    FROM catalog_sales
    INNER JOIN date_filter ON cs_sold_date_sk = date_filter.d_date_sk
    INNER JOIN catalog_page ON cs_catalog_page_sk = cp_catalog_page_sk
    INNER JOIN item ON cs_item_sk = i_item_sk
    INNER JOIN promotion ON cs_promo_sk = p_promo_sk
    LEFT JOIN catalog_returns
           ON cs_item_sk = cr_item_sk AND cs_order_number = cr_order_number
    WHERE i_current_price > 50
      AND p_channel_email = 'N'
      AND p_channel_tv = 'N'
      AND p_channel_radio = 'Y'
      AND p_channel_press = 'N'
      AND p_channel_event = 'Y'
      AND cs_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 45 AND 60
      AND i_category IN ('Jewelry', 'Sports')
    GROUP BY cp_catalog_page_id
),
wsr AS (
    SELECT web_site_id,
           SUM(ws_ext_sales_price) AS sales,
           SUM(COALESCE(wr_return_amt, 0)) AS returns,
           SUM(ws_net_profit - COALESCE(wr_net_loss, 0)) AS profit
    FROM web_sales
    INNER JOIN date_filter ON ws_sold_date_sk = date_filter.d_date_sk
    INNER JOIN web_site ON ws_web_site_sk = web_site_sk
    INNER JOIN item ON ws_item_sk = i_item_sk
    INNER JOIN promotion ON ws_promo_sk = p_promo_sk
    LEFT JOIN web_returns
           ON ws_item_sk = wr_item_sk AND ws_order_number = wr_order_number
    WHERE i_current_price > 50
      AND p_channel_email = 'N'
      AND p_channel_tv = 'N'
      AND p_channel_radio = 'Y'
      AND p_channel_press = 'N'
      AND p_channel_event = 'Y'
      AND ws_wholesale_cost BETWEEN 45 AND 60
      AND i_category IN ('Jewelry', 'Sports')
    GROUP BY web_site_id
)
SELECT channel,
       id,
       SUM(sales) AS sales,
       SUM(returns) AS returns,
       SUM(profit) AS profit
FROM (
    SELECT 'store channel' AS channel, 'store' || store_id AS id, sales, returns, profit FROM ssr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'catalog channel', 'catalog_page' || catalog_page_id, sales, returns, profit FROM csr
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'web channel', 'web_site' || web_site_id, sales, returns, profit FROM wsr
) x
GROUP BY ROLLUP (channel, id)
ORDER BY channel, id
LIMIT 100;

Equivalent since BETWEEN is inclusive of the 30th day.

Introduced a materialized `date_filter` CTE (referenced 3 times). The date range yields ~31 rows out of 73,049, so computing it once and reusing it eliminates three full index scans of date_dim (~cost 3057 each).

Converted implicit comma joins mixed with LEFT OUTER JOIN into explicit INNER JOIN / LEFT JOIN syntax, and reordered joins so dimension inner joins happen before the returns LEFT JOIN. Semantically equivalent because inner-join conditions reference only the sales side.

Kept return tables as LEFT JOINs (no return-date filtering allowed) and kept the ROLLUP/LIMIT structure unchanged — the outer aggregation is required for channel/grand subtotals; planner cost (~52k) shows this region is already cheap.

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace `cast('1999-09-24' as date) + interval '30' day` with the pre-computed inclusive upper bound `date '1999-10-24'`, simplifying the date predicate in all three CTEs without changing semantics.

WITH customer_total_return AS (
    SELECT

        ca_state AS ctr_state,

    FROM catalog_returns
    JOIN date_dim
      ON cr_returned_date_sk = d_date_sk
    JOIN customer_address
      ON cr_returning_addr_sk = ca_address_sk
    WHERE d_year = 1998
    GROUP BY cr_returning_customer_sk, ca_state
),
state_return_threshold AS (
    SELECT
        ctr_state,
        AVG(ctr_total_return) * 1.2 AS avg_threshold
    FROM customer_total_return
    GROUP BY ctr_state
)
SELECT
    c.c_customer_id,
    c.c_salutation,
    c.c_first_name,
    c.c_last_name,
    ca.ca_street_number,
    ca.ca_street_name,

    ca.ca_state,

    ca.ca_gmt_offset,
    ca.ca_location_type,
    ctr1.ctr_total_return
FROM customer_total_return ctr1
JOIN state_return_threshold s
  ON ctr1.ctr_state = s.ctr_state
JOIN customer c
  ON ctr1.ctr_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
WHERE ctr1.ctr_total_return > s.avg_threshold

    ca.ca_state,
    ca.ca_zip,

    ctr1.ctr_total_return
LIMIT 100;

WITH target_dates AS (
    SELECT d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq IN (
        SELECT d_month_seq
        FROM date_dim
        WHERE d_date IN (DATE '1999-03-22', DATE '1999-05-27', DATE '1999-08-04', DATE '1999-11-10')
    )
),
eligible_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_item_id
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Shoes', 'Women')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 3 AND 12
      AND i_item_id IS NOT NULL
),
all_returns AS (
    SELECT 'S'::text AS src, sr.sr_item_sk AS item_sk, sr.sr_return_quantity AS return_qty
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN target_dates d ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE sr.sr_reason_sk IN (3, 4, 26, 40, 52)
      AND sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 264 AND 293
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'C'::text, cr.cr_item_sk, cr.cr_return_quantity
    FROM catalog_returns cr
    JOIN target_dates d ON cr.cr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE cr.cr_reason_sk IN (3, 4, 26, 40, 52)
      AND cr.cr_return_amount / cr.cr_return_quantity BETWEEN 264 AND 293
    UNION ALL
    SELECT 'W'::text, wr.wr_item_sk, wr.wr_return_quantity
    FROM web_returns wr
    JOIN target_dates d ON wr.wr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE wr.wr_reason_sk IN (3, 4, 26, 40, 52)
      AND wr.wr_return_amt / wr.wr_return_quantity BETWEEN 264 AND 293
),
agg AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           SUM(CASE WHEN r.src = 'S' THEN r.return_qty END) AS sr_item_qty,
           SUM(CASE WHEN r.src = 'C' THEN r.return_qty END) AS cr_item_qty,
           SUM(CASE WHEN r.src = 'W' THEN r.return_qty END) AS wr_item_qty
    FROM all_returns r
    JOIN eligible_items i ON r.item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id
    HAVING COUNT(CASE WHEN r.src = 'S' THEN 1 END) > 0
       AND COUNT(CASE WHEN r.src = 'C' THEN 1 END) > 0
       AND COUNT(CASE WHEN r.src = 'W' THEN 1 END) > 0
)
SELECT item_id,
       sr_item_qty,
       sr_item_qty / (sr_item_qty + cr_item_qty + wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS sr_dev,
       cr_item_qty,
       cr_item_qty / (sr_item_qty + cr_item_qty + wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS cr_dev,
       wr_item_qty,
       wr_item_qty / (sr_item_qty + cr_item_qty + wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS wr_dev,

FROM agg
ORDER BY item_id, sr_item_qty
LIMIT 100;

Replace three separate GROUP BY aggregations plus a 3-way inner join with a UNION ALL of the three return streams and one GROUP BY using conditional aggregation. The HAVING COUNT(...) > 0 conditions enforce the original inner-join semantics (item must have returns in all three channels).

Added i_item_id IS NOT NULL to eligible_items to exactly preserve the original behavior where NULL item_id rows could not survive the final equality joins. The non-sargable return-amount/quantity ratio predicates were preserved as-is to maintain strict semantic equivalence.
