rewritten_query:
WITH target_dates AS (
    SELECT d1.d_date_sk
    FROM date_dim d1
    WHERE d1.d_month_seq IN (
        SELECT d2.d_month_seq
        FROM date_dim d2
        WHERE d2.d_date IN (DATE '2002-02-09', DATE '2002-04-16', DATE '2002-07-16', DATE '2002-10-28')
    )
),
filtered_items AS (
    SELECT i_item_sk, i_item_id
    FROM item
    WHERE i_category IN ('Home', 'Jewelry')
      AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 91 AND 100
),
sr_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           SUM(sr.sr_return_quantity) AS sr_item_qty
    FROM store_returns sr
    JOIN target_dates d ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_items i ON sr.sr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE sr.sr_reason_sk IN (3, 20, 40, 43, 51)
      AND sr.sr_return_amt / sr.sr_return_quantity BETWEEN 271 AND 300
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id
),
cr_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           SUM(cr.cr_return_quantity) AS cr_item_qty
    FROM catalog_returns cr
    JOIN target_dates d ON cr.cr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_items i ON cr.cr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE cr.cr_reason_sk IN (3, 20, 40, 43, 51)
      AND cr.cr_return_amount / cr.cr_return_quantity BETWEEN 271 AND 300
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id
),
wr_items AS (
    SELECT i.i_item_id AS item_id,
           SUM(wr.wr_return_quantity) AS wr_item_qty
    FROM web_returns wr
    JOIN target_dates d ON wr.wr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    JOIN filtered_items i ON wr.wr_item_sk = i.i_item_sk
    WHERE wr.wr_reason_sk IN (3, 20, 40, 43, 51)
      AND wr.wr_return_amt / wr.wr_return_quantity BETWEEN 271 AND 300
    GROUP BY i.i_item_id
)
SELECT sr_items.item_id,
       sr_items.sr_item_qty,
       sr_items.sr_item_qty / (sr_items.sr_item_qty + cr_items.cr_item_qty + wr_items.wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS sr_dev,
       cr_items.cr_item_qty,
       cr_items.cr_item_qty / (sr_items.sr_item_qty + cr_items.cr_item_qty + wr_items.wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS cr_dev,
       wr_items.wr_item_qty,
       wr_items.wr_item_qty / (sr_items.sr_item_qty + cr_items.cr_item_qty + wr_items.wr_item_qty) / 3.0 * 100 AS wr_dev,
       (sr_items.sr_item_qty + cr_items.cr_item_qty + wr_items.wr_item_qty) / 3.0 AS average
FROM sr_items
JOIN cr_items ON sr_items.item_id = cr_items.item_id
JOIN wr_items ON sr_items.item_id = wr_items.item_id
ORDER BY sr_items.item_id, sr_items.sr_item_qty
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: The nested date_dim self-subquery (d_date IN (... d_month_seq IN (...))) was repeated three times. It is computed once in a target_dates CTE. Since d_date is unique in date_dim, filtering by d_month_seq directly is equivalent and avoids the repeated d_date semi-join.
The common item filters (i_category IN ('Home','Jewelry') AND i_manager_id BETWEEN 91 AND 100) were extracted into a single filtered_items CTE reused by all three return channels.
Old-style comma joins were converted to explicit INNER JOINs, improving readability and giving the optimizer clearer join predicates.
The final three-way cross join with WHERE equality was rewritten as explicit joins. The final join operates on small aggregated CTEs, so no UNION ALL conditional aggregation was introduced.

FROM customer c
JOIN customer_address ca ON c.c_current_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk

JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk

 customer_demographics cd2, customer_address, date_dim, reason  where ws_web_page_sk = wp_web_page_sk    and ws_item_sk = wr_item_sk    and ws_order_number = wr_order_number    and ws_sold_date_sk = and    (     (      cd1.cd_marital_status = 'W'      and      cd1.cd_marital_status = cd2.cd_marital_status      and      cd1.cd_education_status = '2 yr Degree'      and      cd1.cd_education_status = cd2.cd_education_status      and      ws_sales_price between 100.00 and 150.00     )    or     (      cd1.cd_marital_status = 'S'      and      cd1.cd_marital_status = cd2.cd_marital_status      and      cd1.cd_education_status = 'College'      and      cd1.cd_education_status = cd2.cd_education_status      and      ws_sales_price between 50.00 and 100.00     )    or     (      cd1.cd_marital_status = 'D'      and      cd1.cd_marital_status = cd2.cd_marital_status      and      cd1.cd_education_status = 'Advanced Degree'      and      cd1.cd_education_status = ca_country = 'United States'      and      ca_state in ('GA', 'IL', 'OH')      and ws_net_profit between 50 and 250     )    ) group by r_reason_desc order by substring(r_reason_desc,1,20)         ,avg(ws_quantity)         ,avg(wr_refunded_cash)         ,avg(wr_fee) limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH demo_ranges (cd_marital_status, cd_education_status, min_price, max_price) AS (
    VALUES
        ('W'::bpchar, '2 yr Degree'::bpchar, 100.00::numeric, 150.00::numeric),
        ('S'::bpchar, 'College'::bpchar, 50.00::numeric, 100.00::numeric),
        ('D'::bpchar, 'Advanced Degree'::bpchar, 150.00::numeric, 200.00::numeric)
),
addr_ranges (ca_state, min_profit, max_profit) AS (
    VALUES
        ('GA'::bpchar, 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('IN'::bpchar, 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('VA'::bpchar, 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        ('MT'::bpchar, 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('NM'::bpchar, 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('OR'::bpchar, 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        ('IL'::bpchar, 50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        ('OH'::bpchar, 50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        ('GA'::bpchar, 50::numeric, 250::numeric)
),
sales_1998 AS (
    SELECT ws.ws_item_sk,
           ws.ws_order_number,
           ws.ws_web_page_sk,
           ws.ws_quantity,
           ws.ws_sales_price,
           ws.ws_net_profit
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d
      ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
    WHERE d.d_year = 1998
      AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00
      AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300
)
SELECT substring(r.r_reason_desc, 1, 20) AS reason_desc_20,
       avg(ws.ws_quantity) AS avg_qty,
       avg(wr.wr_refunded_cash) AS avg_refunded_cash,
       avg(wr.wr_fee) AS avg_fee
FROM sales_1998 ws
JOIN web_returns wr
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = wr.wr_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_order_number = wr.wr_order_number
JOIN customer_demographics cd1
  ON wr.wr_refunded_cdemo_sk = cd1.cd_demo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd2
  ON wr.wr_returning_cdemo_sk = cd2.cd_demo_sk
 AND cd2.cd_marital_status = cd1.cd_marital_status
 AND cd2.cd_education_status = cd1.cd_education_status
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON wr.wr_refunded_addr_sk = ca.ca_address_sk
 AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
JOIN web_page wp
  ON ws.ws_web_page_sk = wp.wp_web_page_sk
JOIN reason r
  ON wr.wr_reason_sk = r.r_reason_sk
WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM demo_ranges dr
        WHERE cd1.cd_marital_status = dr.cd_marital_status
          AND cd1.cd_education_status = dr.cd_education_status
          AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN dr.min_price AND dr.max_price
      )
  AND EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM addr_ranges ar
        WHERE ca.ca_state = ar.ca_state
          AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN ar.min_profit AND ar.max_profit
      )
GROUP BY r.r_reason_desc
ORDER BY reason_desc_20,
         avg_qty,
         avg_refunded_cash,
         avg_fee
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Factored the common ca_country='United States' out of the three OR branches and merged the overlapping GA ranges (100-200 ∪ 50-250 → 50-250) into a single state-to-profit-range mapping, replacing large OR chains with clean range joins.

Replaced repeated equality chains (cd1.cd_marital_status = cd2.cd_marital_status AND cd1.cd_education_status = cd2.cd_education_status inside each OR branch) with a demo_ranges mapping CTE joined once, and pushed the d_year=1998 date filter into a sales_1998 pre-filtered CTE.

Added redundant-but-useful overall range prefilters on web_sales (ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50 AND 200, ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300), which are the union of all branch ranges and safe, allowing early row reduction on the 7.2M-row web_sales table before joining.

Converted implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI INNER JOINs and moved filter predicates into the corresponding JOIN ON clauses; ordered joins so filtered/prefiltered relations (sales_1998, mapped demographics and address) drive the join order.

Folded the union of the three sales-price branch ranges into one constant prefilter (50–200) and the union of the three net-profit ranges into (50–300); merged GA's overlapping state range sets into a single constant range 50–250.

WITH allowed_demo(ms, es, price_lo, price_hi) AS (
    VALUES
        (CAST('U' AS char(1)), CAST('Primary' AS char(15)), 100.00, 150.00),
        (CAST('D' AS char(1)), CAST('4 yr Degree' AS char(15)), 50.00, 100.00),
        (CAST('M' AS char(1)), CAST('College' AS char(15)), 150.00, 200.00)
),
allowed_state_profit(state, profit_lo, profit_hi) AS (
    VALUES
        (CAST('NE' AS char(2)), 100::numeric, 200::numeric),
        (CAST('TN' AS char(2)),  50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        (CAST('TX' AS char(2)),  50::numeric, 250::numeric),
        (CAST('MS' AS char(2)),  50::numeric, 300::numeric),
        (CAST('NY' AS char(2)), 150::numeric, 300::numeric),
        (CAST('VA' AS char(2)), 150::numeric, 300::numeric)
)
SELECT substring(r.r_reason_desc, 1, 20) AS reason_desc_20,
       avg(ws.ws_quantity) AS avg_ws_quantity,
       avg(wr.wr_refunded_cash) AS avg_refunded_cash,
       avg(wr.wr_fee) AS avg_fee
FROM web_sales ws
JOIN date_dim d
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
 AND d.d_year = 1999
JOIN web_page wp
  ON ws.ws_web_page_sk = wp.wp_web_page_sk
JOIN web_returns wr
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = wr.wr_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_order_number = wr.wr_order_number
JOIN customer_demographics cd1
  ON cd1.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_refunded_cdemo_sk
JOIN allowed_demo ad
  ON cd1.cd_marital_status = ad.ms
 AND cd1.cd_education_status = ad.es
 AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN ad.price_lo AND ad.price_hi
JOIN customer_demographics cd2
  ON cd2.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_returning_cdemo_sk
 AND cd2.cd_marital_status = ad.ms
 AND cd2.cd_education_status = ad.es
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = wr.wr_refunded_addr_sk
JOIN allowed_state_profit asp
  ON ca.ca_state = asp.state
 AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN asp.profit_lo AND asp.profit_hi
JOIN reason r
  ON r.r_reason_sk = wr.wr_reason_sk
WHERE ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00
  AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300
GROUP BY r.r_reason_desc
ORDER BY reason_desc_20,
         avg_ws_quantity,
         avg_refunded_cash,
         avg_fee
LIMIT 100;

Replaced the large OR blocks with tiny VALUES-based mapping CTEs (allowed_demo, allowed_state_profit) joined as small hash-join build sides, converting late-applied join filters into equi-join conditions.

Converted implicit comma joins to explicit ANSI JOINs, and added safe broad pre-filters ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50 AND 200 and ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300 (union of all branch ranges) to enable earlier filtering of web_sales (7.2M rows). ORDER BY uses output aliases. The web_page join is retained for strict equivalence; if TPC-DS FK integrity is guaranteed it can be dropped as wp columns are unreferenced.

Join conditions embedded in ORs were made explicit join keys (cd2 joined to the allowed_demo mapping), letting the planner hash-join against 3-row and 6-row mapping tables instead of evaluating complex OR join filters.

       avg(ws.ws_quantity),
       avg(wr.wr_refunded_cash),

JOIN web_returns wr
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = wr.wr_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_order_number = wr.wr_order_number
JOIN web_page wp
  ON ws.ws_web_page_sk = wp.wp_web_page_sk
JOIN date_dim d
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
 AND d.d_year = 2000
JOIN customer_demographics cd1
  ON cd1.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_refunded_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd2
  ON cd2.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_returning_cdemo_sk
 AND cd2.cd_marital_status = cd1.cd_marital_status
 AND cd2.cd_education_status = cd1.cd_education_status
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = wr.wr_refunded_addr_sk

JOIN reason r

WHERE (
        (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'D' AND cd1.cd_education_status = 'Primary'   AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 100.00 AND 150.00)
     OR (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'S' AND cd1.cd_education_status = 'College'   AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 100.00)
     OR (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'U' AND cd1.cd_education_status = '2 yr Degree' AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 150.00 AND 200.00)
      )

        (ca.ca_state IN ('FL', 'WI')         AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 200)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('MO', 'NC', 'PA')   AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 150 AND 300)

      )

Converted implicit comma joins to explicit INNER JOIN syntax and pushed constant filters (d_year = 2000, ca_country = 'United States', cd2 equalities) into ON clauses, enabling earlier filtering during join execution.

Rejected a VALUES/CTE mapping join approach: it adds an extra join operator (the prior rewrite raised cost from ~92193 to ~99290). The simplified in-place OR predicates preserve the original plan shape while reducing filter complexity.

    MIN(cd2.cd_demo_sk)      AS min_cd2_demo_sk
FROM web_sales ws
JOIN web_returns wr
  ON ws.ws_item_sk = wr.wr_item_sk
 AND ws.ws_order_number = wr.wr_order_number
JOIN web_page wp
  ON ws.ws_web_page_sk = wp.wp_web_page_sk
JOIN date_dim d
  ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk

JOIN customer_demographics cd1
  ON cd1.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_refunded_cdemo_sk

  ON cd2.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_returning_cdemo_sk
 AND cd2.cd_marital_status = cd1.cd_marital_status
 AND cd2.cd_education_status = cd1.cd_education_status
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = wr.wr_refunded_addr_sk
 AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
 AND ca.ca_state IN ('GA','IN','VA','MT','NM','OR','IL','OH')

WHERE (
        (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'W'

     OR (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'S'
         AND cd1.cd_education_status = 'College'
         AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 100.00)
     OR (cd1.cd_marital_status = 'D'
         AND cd1.cd_education_status = 'Advanced Degree'
         AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN 150.00 AND 200.00)
      )
  AND (
        (ca.ca_state IN ('IN','VA')        AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 100 AND 200)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('MT','NM','OR')   AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 150 AND 300)
     OR (ca.ca_state IN ('GA','IL','OH')   AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50  AND 250)

This is valid for inner joins and reduces OR complexity.

Removed the redundant 'GA' overlap in the second OR group: for GA, the branch with net_profit 100-200 is fully subsumed by the branch with net_profit 50-250, so GA was removed from the first branch. This makes the state sets ({IN,VA}, {MT,NM,OR}, {GA,IL,OH}) mutually exclusive and simplifies OR evaluation.

Added implied overall range filters: ws_sales_price BETWEEN 50.00 AND 200.00 (union of the three price branches) and ws_net_profit BETWEEN 50 AND 300 (union of the three profit branches). These are logically implied, cost-free to add, and allow earlier filtering of web_sales rows before OR evaluation.

Converted the comma-join syntax to explicit ANSI JOINs with a deterministic join tree, and pushed dimension filters (d_year, ca_country, ca_state IN union of all branch states) into JOIN ON clauses to enable earlier filtering of small dimension tables before joining to the large fact tables.

Additional recommendation (not expressible in SQL rewrite alone): create supporting indexes — customer_demographics(cd_marital_status, cd_education_status) INCLUDE (cd_demo_sk) to replace the expensive 1.9M-row seq scan for cd1; web_returns(wr_refunded_cdemo_sk) and web_returns(wr_refunded_addr_sk) to enable index-based joins from the filtered dimensions instead of a full 1.4M-row scan.

    min(wr.wr_refunded_cash)  AS min_wr_refunded_cash,

    min(ws.ws_item_sk)        AS min_ws_item_sk,
    min(wr.wr_order_number)   AS min_wr_order_number,
    min(cd1.cd_demo_sk)       AS min_cd1_demo_sk,

JOIN web_page wp
    ON ws.ws_web_page_sk = wp.wp_web_page_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd1
    ON cd1.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_refunded_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd2
    ON cd2.cd_demo_sk = wr.wr_returning_cdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca

JOIN date_dim d
    ON ws.ws_sold_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
JOIN reason r
    ON r.r_reason_sk = wr.wr_reason_sk
JOIN sales_conditions sc

JOIN address_conditions ac
    ON ca.ca_state = ac.ca_state
WHERE d.d_year = 1999
  AND ca.ca_country = 'United States'
  AND cd2.cd_marital_status  = cd1.cd_marital_status
  AND cd2.cd_education_status = cd1.cd_education_status
  AND ws.ws_sales_price BETWEEN sc.price_min AND sc.price_max
  AND ws.ws_net_profit BETWEEN ac.profit_min AND ac.profit_max;

SELECT cc.cc_call_center_id Call_Center,
       cc.cc_name Call_Center_Name,
       cc.cc_manager Manager,
       SUM(cr.cr_net_loss) Returns_Loss
FROM date_dim d
JOIN catalog_returns cr ON cr.cr_returned_date_sk = d.d_date_sk
JOIN call_center cc ON cr.cr_call_center_sk = cc.cc_call_center_sk
JOIN customer c ON cr.cr_returning_customer_sk = c.c_customer_sk
JOIN customer_demographics cd ON cd.cd_demo_sk = c.c_current_cdemo_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
JOIN customer_address ca ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
WHERE d.d_year = 1999
  AND d.d_moy = 3
  AND (cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status) IN (('M','Unknown'), ('W','Advanced Degree'))
  AND hd.hd_buy_potential LIKE '>10000%'
  AND ca.ca_gmt_offset = -7
GROUP BY cc.cc_call_center_id, cc.cc_name, cc.cc_manager, cd.cd_marital_status, cd.cd_education_status
ORDER BY SUM(cr.cr_net_loss) DESC;

WITH date_range AS (
    SELECT MIN(d_date_sk) AS min_date_sk,
           MAX(d_date_sk) AS max_date_sk
    FROM date_dim
    WHERE d_month_seq BETWEEN 1193 AND 1216
),
filtered_sales AS NOT MATERIALIZED (
    SELECT
        SUBSTRING(w.w_warehouse_name, 1, 20) AS warehouse_name,
        sm.sm_type,
        cc.cc_name,
        cs.cs_ship_date_sk - cs.cs_sold_date_sk AS days_to_ship
    FROM catalog_sales cs
    JOIN date_range dr
      ON cs.cs_ship_date_sk BETWEEN dr.min_date_sk AND dr.max_date_sk
    JOIN ship_mode sm
      ON cs.cs_ship_mode_sk = sm.sm_ship_mode_sk
    JOIN warehouse w
      ON cs.cs_warehouse_sk = w.w_warehouse_sk
    JOIN call_center cc
      ON cs.cs_call_center_sk = cc.cc_call_center_sk
    WHERE cs.cs_list_price BETWEEN 77 AND 106
      AND sm.sm_type = 'TWO DAY'
      AND cc.cc_class = 'small'
      AND w.w_gmt_offset = -5
)
SELECT
    warehouse_name,
    sm_type,
    cc_name,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_ship <= 30) AS "30 days",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_ship > 30 AND days_to_ship <= 60) AS "31-60 days",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_ship > 60 AND days_to_ship <= 90) AS "61-90 days",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_ship > 90 AND days_to_ship <= 120) AS "91-120 days",
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_ship > 120) AS ">120 days"
FROM filtered_sales
GROUP BY warehouse_name, sm_type, cc_name
ORDER BY warehouse_name, sm_type, cc_name
LIMIT 100;

rewritten_query:
SELECT
    c.c_customer_sk,
    c.c_first_name,
    c.c_last_name,
    CAST(SUM(ws_match.cnt) AS bigint) AS cnt
FROM store_returns sr
JOIN date_dim d1
  ON d1.d_date_sk = sr.sr_returned_date_sk
JOIN item i
  ON i.i_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN store_sales ss
  ON ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
 AND ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
JOIN customer c
  ON c.c_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
JOIN customer_address ca
  ON ca.ca_address_sk = c.c_current_addr_sk
JOIN household_demographics hd
  ON hd.hd_demo_sk = c.c_current_hdemo_sk
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM web_sales ws
    JOIN date_dim d2
      ON d2.d_date_sk = ws.ws_sold_date_sk
    WHERE ws.ws_bill_customer_sk = ss.ss_customer_sk
      AND ws.ws_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
      AND d2.d_date BETWEEN d1.d_date AND d1.d_date + INTERVAL '90' day
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 0
) ws_match
WHERE d1.d_year = 1999
  AND i.i_category IN ('Books', 'Shoes', 'Sports')
  AND ss.ss_sales_price >= 0.80 * ss.ss_list_price
  AND ss.ss_sales_price <= 1.00 * ss.ss_list_price
  AND ca.ca_state IN ('IN', 'MT', 'NM', 'OH', 'OR')
  AND hd.hd_income_band_sk BETWEEN 14 AND 20
  AND hd.hd_buy_potential = '5001-10000'
GROUP BY
    c.c_customer_sk,
    c.c_first_name,
    c.c_last_name
ORDER BY cnt;

HAVING COUNT(*) > 0 preserves inner-join semantics; this reduces intermediate rows and is the most impactful rewrite (score 5/5).

Replace the division filter ss_sales_price/ss_list_price BETWEEN 0.80 AND 1.00 with multiplication form ss_sales_price BETWEEN 0.80*ss_list_price AND 1.00*ss_list_price, avoiding per-row division and possible numeric casts (valid for positive list prices as in TPC-DS; score 3/5).

Push selective dimension filters (d_year=1999, i_category, ca_state, hd filters) into explicit WHERE/JOIN clauses; avoid materialized CTEs since all subqueries are used once and PostgreSQL can inline them (score 2/5).
